report:
Session 2 done: added src/export.py, following docs/PROJECT_RULES.md (read first).

What was built
- export_report(rows, path): public, name ends with _report (rule 2), one-line docstring (rule 5). Writes a "Ledger" sheet: header date, amount; one line per (date, amount) row; then a summary line from summarize_report in src/report.py. Returns the path. Refuses a path not ending in .xlsx.
- _format_date(value): private helper, no _report suffix (correction 9). Returns the date as ISO YYYY-MM-DD (rule 7), reusing report._to_iso_date, so non-ISO strings and datetimes are refused.
- _read_rows(csv_path): private helper for the CLI; opens the input with encoding="utf-8" (rule 6).
- main(argv=None): CLI. Usage: python -m src.export input.csv output.xlsx (input CSV has a date,amount header). Prints the written path; print only inside main (rule 1, correction 7). Logging elsewhere.
- Amounts go through report._to_decimal, so floats are refused (rule 4).
- Dependency: openpyxl only, which the owner approved (correction 9). No other dependency added. No requirements file exists in the folder, so none was edited.

Checked
- CLI run on a 2-row CSV wrote the file and printed its path. Read back: header, 2026-10-01 / 12.5, 2026-10-02 / 7.25, blank, summary "2 rows, total 19.75".
- A float amount raises TypeError; a date "10/01/2026" raises ValueError.

Open
- An .xlsx number cell is stored as a binary double, so reading the amount back gives a float (12.5), even though Decimal goes in. If money must stay exact in the file too, the amount could be written as text instead. That is the owner's choice; not changed.
